name: Bilba
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 3 other works consulted do not discuss stress.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: Quote verified verbatim in a copy consulted of the deciding source (Edwards 2021 p.35), which the record failed to link because the PDF sits under term1237/src rather than bilb1242 (we have no copy and grade/cite/loc fields empty). The source is a 2021 specialist synthesis by an author with his own Bilbaa field data, and the only older description in scope (Jonker 1915 sec. 4, held) states the same penult rule with no suffix-induced shift. Nothing Bilba-specific and nothing better exists per Glottolog (0 descriptive refs) and the reachable web. Coding 'penult primary, alternating secondary leftward' (stress placement coded per word length as 10 010 1010 01010 (1 = a stressed syllable)) matches the quote exactly. Weakness is only that the statement is cluster-level (all Rote lects) from a dictionary's background chapter rather than a Bilba phonology, hence 'adequate' not 'well-sourced'. sources.citation: Edwards 2021, Rote-Meto Comparative Dictionary, ANU Press, section 2.4 phonology of the Rote varieties incl. Bilbaa (full PDF re-read)
sources.quote: Content words contain at least two vowels. Some functors, such as the conjunction ma ‘and’, are monosyllabic. Stress falls on the penultimate vowel of a word with secondary stress assigned to every second syllable to the left.

sources.citation: Fox, James J. and Charles E. Grimes. 1995. Roti: introduction and wordlist. In Darrell T. Tryon (ed.), Comparative Austronesian Dictionary, Part 1 Fascicle 1, 611-622. Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter.
sources.access_detail: open copy posted by the author (located 2026-09-25); a digital copy (available on request)
sources.quote: Jonker (1913), following Manafe (1889), distinguished eight dialects: three eastern dialects (Bilba, Ringgou and Korbaffo); two central dialects (Termanu - known locally as Pada - and Ba'a); and three western dialects (Tii - given Dutch spelling as Thie -, Dengka and Oenale). [...] Differences between dialects are not only lexical, but also phonological with different dialects manifesting different historical sound correspondences. [...] Most of the early studies of Rotinese were in the dialects of Termanu and Ba'a. Jonker chose the dialect of Termanu as the basis for his dictionary and grammar. Fox has also concentrated on the Termanu dialect in his studies of ritual language.
sources.locator: printed p. 613; stress statement printed p. 614, section 2.3
sources.note: This work describes Roti (Rotinese) as one language with an eight-dialect chain; the phonological data are Termanu-based (Fox's Termanu field corpus; consonant notes are stated for the Termanu dialect). Bilba is named only as one of the three eastern dialects. Indirect only. The work treats Bilba as an eastern dialect of Roti and gives one unqualified stress statement for 'Roti' (penultimate syllable of the root, primary on the final root of compounds, secondary marked on the earlier root), which agrees with the catalog's penultimate primary for Bilba (cite Edwards 2021).
